newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle market quiet, no sales - trade.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle market quiet, no sales - trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Monday were quiet, with no sales expected until Tuesday or Wednesday, feedlot sources said.
Cattle owners were asking $68.00 and expected to see packer bids at $66.00 before trading at $67.00, they said.
There were light sales Friday at $67.00, down $1.00 from brisk volume earlier in the week.
Weakness in the market was attributed to declines in beef prices last week and projections for increased feedlot cattle supplies starting the next few weeks, market sources said.
Beef prices Friday were quoted down $0.22 to $0.56, USDA said. The choice heavyweight price was down $0.32 at $107.98, down $6.96 for the week.
However, the lower prices attracted strong movement, with 366 fabricated loads sold on Friday.
Showlists this week were seen steady to slightly larger than last week, but still with a fair number of unfinished or "green" cattle, they said.
